reviewed_files: pte-api/app/src/test/java/com/pte/overview|identity|tenancy|attempt|billing|support/... Phase 3 test classes (file list and report method inventory only)

findings.evidence: UserRepository: '@Query("select u.tenantId, count(u.id) from User u join u.roles r where r = :role and u.deleted = false and u.tenantId is not null group by u.tenantId")' with Javadoc 'each user matches at most once and a plain count is exact'. V2__identity.sql: 'CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS user_roles (user_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES users (id), role VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL);' preceded by the comment 'no synthetic PK'; the only index on (user_id, role) is the NON-unique idx_user_roles_user_role (V4). phase-03-explain-plans.txt:37-38 and the IT comment at OverviewMigrationPostgresIntegrationTest.java:496 state 'user_roles is unique per (user_id, role)'. The sibling tenant-scoped counts (countByTenantIdAndRole, countByTenantIdAndRoleGroupedByStatus, countByTenantIdAndRoleCreatedBetween, UserRepository.java:108-123) still use count(distinct u.id), and countByTenantIdAndRole feeds quota enforcement.
findings.why_it_matters: Exactness verified under the application invariant: User.roles is a Set<Role> element collection (User.java:69-73), the join is filtered to a single role (r = :role), so Hibernate's Set write path yields at most one STUDENT row per user, and V35/V89 explicitly de-duplicated historical rows. So count(u.id) equals count(distinct u.id) today, and the sort/spill removal is valid (~95 ms -> ~45 ms at 100k students). But the database does not enforce it: a duplicate row (raw SQL, future migration) would inflate this dashboard figure while quota enforcement (count distinct) stays correct, and the platform total would silently diverge from the quota view. The Javadoc/EXPLAIN claim of DB-level uniqueness is stronger than the schema. Severity lowered from the rule default (HIGH) because it only affects a read-only dashboard metric, never authorization or quota.
findings.required_action: Non-blocking. Reword the Javadoc/IT comment to state the real basis (Set element collection + de-duplicating migrations, no DB constraint), and consider a separate migration adding a UNIQUE index on user_roles (user_id, role) (which would also serve the index-only scan suggested in the EXPLAIN notes).

findings.evidence: public long countDistinctActiveStudents(UUID tenantId, Instant from, Instant to) { ... }  and  public long countDistinctActiveStudents(Instant from, Instant to) { return attemptRepository.countDistinctStudentsStartedBetweenPlatformWide(from, to); }  -- same public method name on a root facade, one tenant-scoped, one platform-wide; Javadoc warns 'Not tenant-scoped, so only platform dashboards may call it'.
findings.why_it_matters: The repository method is correctly named ...PlatformWide, but the facade overload hides the scope difference in the arity alone. A tenant-scoped caller (HostDashboardService.java:96 style) that drops or mis-orders the tenantId argument still compiles and silently returns platform-wide data on a tenant dashboard - a cross-tenant disclosure that a distinct name would make a compile error. The facade is public at the module root, so any module can call either variant.
findings.required_action: Non-blocking. Rename the platform overload to something like countDistinctActiveStudentsPlatformWide (and update AdminTenantSections.java:63-64).

findings.evidence: The captured primary entry 'students per tenant' is 'select u.tenant_id, count(distinct u.id) ...' (Seq Scan + Sort external merge Disk 3272kB, 95.2 ms); the production query (count(u.id), UserRepository.java:142) is only represented by the entry labelled 'count(*) variant (suggested rewrite, informational)' (HashAggregate, 45.4 ms) which has verdict expectation null. phase-03-test-report.json still lists PERF-001 as an open MEDIUM production concern.
findings.why_it_matters: The change from count(distinct) to count(u.id) was applied after the EXPLAIN capture. The 'variant' plan is a faithful stand-in (u.id is the non-null PK, so count(u.id) = count(*) in Postgres), so the claim is believable, but the stored evidence and the Postgres IT still describe the old query as the real one and the new one as a suggestion, so a future regression back to count(distinct) would not be caught by the IT.
findings.required_action: Non-blocking. Make count(u.id) the primary 'students per tenant' IT entry, keep count(distinct) only as a labelled comparison, re-run the Postgres-gated IT, and mark PERF-001 resolved in the test report.

findings.evidence: TenancyService (quota locking, lifecycle creation, summaries, login lookup) gained five platform-dashboard reads (platformTenantCounts, countTenantsCreatedBetween, countTenantsCreatedPerRange, recentTenants, seatLimits), about 60 lines, leaving the file at 278 of the 300-line limit. Every other module's dashboard reads live in a dedicated facade (IdentityOverviewService, EnrollmentOverviewService, SessionOverviewService, AttemptOverviewService, ScoringOverviewService, ReportingOverviewService, BillingOverviewService, SupportOverviewService). BillingOverviewService now serves two audiences (tenant-scoped host methods and platform-wide admin methods) over five repositories.
findings.why_it_matters: Both files are under 300 lines today and the plan explicitly directs 'tenancy extended on TenancyService' and 'extend the billing and support facades, no parallel facades', and Phase 1 already put countOrganizations on TenancyService, so this is not a violation and no split is required to pass. But Phase 4 (billing revenue summary on the existing billing facade) and Phase 10 (tenant-by-province aggregation and tenant creation in tenancy) will each add to these two files and will push them past 300 lines; the sibling convention is a separate *OverviewService per module.
findings.required_action: Non-blocking. Before Phase 4 / Phase 10 add more methods, extract the dashboard reads into a TenancyOverviewService (root facade, same records) and, if Phase 4 pushes BillingOverviewService past ~300 lines, split its platform-wide half; record the decision against the plan's 'no parallel facades' constraint.

findings.evidence: licenseCounts: 'countGroupedByStatus()' (stored ISSUED/REDEEMED/REVOKED/EXPIRED) then 'issuedValid = max(0, stored ISSUED - countIssuedPastExpiry(now))' and 'expired = stored EXPIRED + issuedPastExpiry' are two separate statements; LicenseCodeRepository.markExpired (line 106-116) flips ISSUED rows past expiry to EXPIRED in the background.
findings.why_it_matters: Under READ COMMITTED an expiry-job commit between the two statements makes those rows count in stored ISSUED (read first) but not in issuedPastExpiry (read second), so issuedValid is briefly overcounted and expired undercounted. The derived-expired rule itself is correct and identical to findAdminPage (ISSUED, code_expires_at not null and <= now; expiringSoon is strictly > now and <= now+7 days). Effect is transient and bounded by the 60 s cache.
findings.required_action: None required. If exactness matters, derive the split in one conditional-aggregate query.

findings.evidence: for (int i = 0; i < boundaries.size() - 1; i++) { counts.add(tenantRepository.countCreatedBetween(boundaries.get(i), boundaries.get(i + 1))); }  -- 12 sequential indexed counts for the growth series, plus 2 window counts and 2 grouped queries in tenants() (16 statements on a cache miss).
findings.why_it_matters: Same accepted pattern as Phase 1 QUAL-006 (portable JPQL, each count <0.1 ms on idx_tenants_created per EXPLAIN, 60 s section cache). Not a defect; revisit only if latency shows up.

findings.evidence: String key = DashboardCacheKeys.admin(visibility.bucket(), window.days(), section.key()); ... cache.getOrCompute(key, OverviewConstants.ADMIN_SECTION_TTL, type, loader)  -- every section, including the window-independent plans, recentTenants and the licenses/subscriptions point-in-time counts, is keyed by windowDays; getOrCompute has no single-flight, so concurrent misses each run the loader.
findings.why_it_matters: Lifecycle is defined and safe (key = scope + schema version + computed bucket + window + section, TTL 60 s, forbidden sections return before any key is built, a loader failure propagates before writeQuietly so a failed section is never cached, Redis failures degrade to compute). Costs are only efficiency: up to 3 identical entries/recomputes per window-independent section, and a thundering herd of the heaviest grouped query on expiry. Matches the plan wording (bucket + window + schema version) and Phase 2 QUAL-005.
findings.required_action: None; optionally drop windowDays from the key of window-independent sections and bump CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION when any cached record shape changes.

findings.evidence: findAllSeatLimits() returns a row per non-deleted tenant and studentCountsByTenant() a map entry per tenant with students (both unbounded, joined in memory by design); recentTenants() calls studentCounts.get() (line 72) - i.e. triggers the whole-platform grouped student query - only to read 5 counts.
findings.why_it_matters: Both result sets grow with the tenant count (4k tenants in the EXPLAIN seed, 50 with students): fine at current and foreseeable scale, and the plan mandates the grouped-count-plus-in-memory-join shape and the per-request Memo. If recentTenants is a cache miss while learners hits (or the reverse) the heavy query still runs for 5 numbers; a bounded IN-query for those 5 tenants would be much cheaper. No N+1: recent tenants = 1 tenant query + 2 billing queries (subscriptions for all ids, plans by id) + the memoized grouped count, and getStudentQuota is never called.
findings.required_action: None; consider a count-by-tenant-ids query for recentTenants if the grouped query ever approaches its 2 s timeout hint.

findings.evidence: totalStudents/totalSeats are summed over seatLimits() (non-deleted tenants only) while activeLearners uses countDistinctStudentsStartedBetweenPlatformWide (a.deleted = false, no tenant filter, so attempts of soft-deleted tenants count). platformTenantCounts: 'if (row[0] == TenantStatus.ACTIVE) ... else if (row[0] == TenantStatus.SUSPENDED)' and PlatformTenantCounts.total() = active + suspended.
findings.why_it_matters: Requirement 'totals only over non-deleted tenants' is met for every total (tenants, students, seats); activeLearners can in theory exceed totalStudents if a deleted tenant's students still have in-window attempts (acknowledged in phase-03-test-report observations). A third TenantStatus value would be dropped from total() silently (TenantStatus has two values today). Both are edge cases, documented in tests.

findings.evidence: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_attempts_submitted ON exam_attempts (submitted_at) WHERE deleted = false;  -- phase-03-test-report.json: 'idx_attempts_submitted (V96) has no production caller yet'. The (status, created_at) indexes on support_ticket / tenant_applications / subscriptions cannot serve the created_at-only range counts (EXPLAIN: default planner Seq Scan, 1.7-4.5 ms at 12-30k rows; license redeemed_at has no index).
findings.why_it_matters: V96 itself is sound: six indexes only, CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS (idempotent, replay verified 12/12 on scratch PG17 from an empty schema), partial on deleted = false like V93-V95, header documents rollback, additive so old and new app versions both work, every heavy V96-targeted query is index-served in the EXPLAIN. Remaining points: (a) idx_attempts_submitted is plan-mandated (Step 3) but speculative and adds write cost on the hottest table; (b) plain CREATE INDEX (not CONCURRENTLY) briefly blocks writes on exam_attempts, same as V94 QUAL-007; (c) PERF-002 (status-less range counts seq-scan) is acceptable: <6 ms at 30k rows, linear, cached 60 s, and the EXPLAIN file records the ~1M-row trigger for created_at-only indexes.
findings.required_action: None; drop or defer idx_attempts_submitted if no admin section consumes it, and add created_at-only partial indexes only when the tables approach ~1M rows.

findings.evidence: TrendCalculator.of(count(w.start(), w.end()), count(w.previousStart(), w.start())) is written out 10 times (6 in Phase 3), each repeating the window arithmetic. TrendCalculator.java:19 still holds the literals 100 and 1 (Phase 1 code); SeatUtilisationRanking correctly names PERCENT / PERCENT_SCALE.
findings.why_it_matters: A mismatched pair (e.g. previousStart/start swapped) would silently skew one trend; a helper on DashboardWindow taking a (from,to) count function would remove the repetition. Not worth a block; the pattern is readable and covered by tests.
findings.required_action: None; optional helper such as TrendCalculator.over(window, counter) when the next section is added.

verification_notes.security_platform_only_access: AdminDashboardController.java:25-44: class-level @PreAuthorize("hasAnyRole('PLATFORM_ADMIN','PLATFORM_MANAGER','ACADEMIC_MANAGER','ACADEMIC_STAFF','PLATFORM_AUTHOR')") (same inline-expression convention as the assessment, itembank and scoretemplate controllers, includes the legacy PLATFORM_AUTHOR token) PLUS an in-method gate: CurrentUserContext.required() then PlatformOperationPolicy.isPlatformCaller(caller) (userId != null, tenantId == null, SecurityPolicy.hasValidScope) else AccessDeniedException(SharedConstants.ACCESS_DENIED) -> 403. HOST_ADMIN and every tenant-bound or tenant-id-carrying caller never reach the service; the controller has no tenant parameter. CurrentUser canonicalizes PLATFORM_AUTHOR to ACADEMIC_STAFF in its compact constructor, so the policy sees the canonical role. SecurityConfig has no dashboard-specific rule and no public path (anyRequest().authenticated(), SecurityConfigDashboardPathTest), so anonymous callers get 401 from the chain.
verification_notes.security_section_table: AdminSection.java:16-23 implemented exactly per the phase table: tenants/learners/recentTenants -> TENANT_READ; applications -> APPLICATION_READ; licenses -> LICENSE_MASKED_READ; subscriptions -> COMMERCIAL_READ; plans -> PLAN_READ_ALL; support -> SUPPORT_READ, each through PlatformOperationPolicy.can (the phase row 'subscriptions, plans -> commercial read / plan read-all' is read as COMMERCIAL_READ for subscriptions and PLAN_READ_ALL for plans, a sound reading that matches MANAGER_OPERATIONS which contains all six). Real policy outcome: PLATFORM_ADMIN and PLATFORM_MANAGER see all 8, ACADEMIC_MANAGER / ACADEMIC_STAFF / legacy PLATFORM_AUTHOR see none (policy is all-or-nothing today).
verification_notes.security_order_and_cache: AdminDashboardService.java:81-89: visibility.allows(section) is evaluated first and returns DashboardSection.forbidden() before DashboardCacheKeys.admin(...) is even called, so a forbidden section is never looked up, computed or cached. The cache key embeds AdminVisibility.bucket() (sorted allowed section keys joined with '+', or 'none'), never a raw role or user id, plus window and section; DashboardCacheKeys.admin rejects a null/blank bucket and the 'admin' scope segment cannot collide with 'host'. An academic caller has an empty allowed set, so no key and no payload; even in a future partial-visibility case the key carries the section name, so an operations section can only be read by a caller whose own checks allowed that section. Partial-bucket paths are exercised only through the key builder (the policy cannot yet produce them) - informational. No secrets: AdminSectionData records carry counts, ids, tenant code/name, plan name, org name/type, requested tenant code, ticket id/category/age only. Queries never read license code values (counts via status/expiry), contact email, tax code, ticket description/submitter or review notes: the entity-returning queries (TenantApplicationRepository.findOldestByStatus, SupportTicketRepository.findOldestByStatus, SubscriptionRepository.findUsableForTenants, TenantRepository.findRecent) load whole rows but the facades map only safe getters (PendingApplicationView, OpenTicketBrief, TenantPlanBrief, RecentTenantView, TenantSeatLimit via JPQL constructor expression). Error responses: DashboardSectionRunner returns a bare ERROR section with the correlation id only in the log.
verification_notes.module_boundaries: overview remains a leaf (no module imports com.pte.overview). New facade surface sits at module roots: tenancy root records TenantSeatLimit / PlatformTenantCounts / RecentTenantView (status as a String, no enum or entity leak), nested records in BillingOverviewService and SupportOverviewService, IdentityOverviewService Map<UUID,Long>, AttemptOverviewService long. overview imports only root types of tenancy, identity, attempt, billing, support (+ shared); package-info allowedDependencies is unchanged by Phase 3 and every listed module is still used (identity by AdminDashboardService, enrollment/session/scoring/reporting by the Host sections). No facade gained a dependency (each uses only its own repositories). Architecture diff: baseline-arch-violations.txt vs after-arch-p3-violations.txt compared entry by entry - the same 7 cycles and the same 11 StudentWorkspaceQueryService 'Allowed targets' lines in a different order; nothing mentions overview, billing, support, tenancy or identity as a new edge. Sizes: all new overview classes <= 91 lines; TenancyService 278 and BillingOverviewService 243 are under 300 (see QUAL-004 for the forward-looking split recommendation).
verification_notes.correctness: Windows: current [now-N, now), previous [now-2N, now-N) (DashboardWindow); active learners = COUNT(DISTINCT studentPublicId) with startedAt in the half-open range and deleted = false, platform-wide, served by idx_attempts_started (bitmap scan ~2.3 ms), previous window the same query. Totals: tenants (status/type counts, created counts) and seat limits filter t.deleted = false; totalStudents is summed over the non-deleted tenant seat-limit list so deleted-tenant students and tenant-less users (u.tenantId is not null) are excluded. SeatUtilisationRanking: cross-multiplied long comparison Long.compare(b.students() * a.seatLimit(), a.students() * b.seatLimit()) is exact (no division, int-sized factors cannot overflow long), ties break by more students then case-insensitive name, then stable input order; limit <= 0 is filtered and limit(Math.max(0, n)); displayed percent is HALF_UP one decimal (ordering never uses the rounded value). Derived-expired license rule equals LicenseCodeRepository.findAdminPage; thresholds are named constants LICENSE_EXPIRING_SOON_DAYS = 7 and EXPIRING_SOON_DAYS = 30 on the billing facade and are echoed in the payload. Months: MonthBuckets.boundaries with OverviewConstants.BUCKET_ZONE_ID (Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh), 12 buckets, last flagged partial, labels from the same YearMonth. Recent tenants: one tenant query, two billing queries (subscriptions IN ids, plans IN ids), the memoized grouped student count; no getStudentQuota/countOrganizations per tenant. Memo: AdminDashboardService.build evaluates the sections strictly sequentially on the caller thread (runner.run -> cache.getOrCompute -> loader.get, no executor), the Memo is created per build() call, so the documented not-thread-safe assumption still holds; a failing grouped count fails both learners and recentTenants independently and is never cached. Jackson: cached payloads are plain records (long, int, double, String, Instant, UUID, Map<String,Long>, List of records, TrendValue) read back by exact class; 56 round-trip tests including the production JsonMapper.
verification_notes.count_distinct_to_count_exactness: Verified at the JPQL/schema level, see QUAL-001: exact while user_roles holds at most one row per (user_id, role), which Hibernate's Set<Role> element collection guarantees on write and V35/V89 enforced on historical data, but which the schema does not enforce (no PK/unique constraint). The H2 test 'multi-role counted once' passes because the join is filtered to one role.
verification_notes.performance: V96: six idempotent, partial (deleted = false), tenant-less indexes; Postgres IT 12/12 on scratch PG17 from an empty schema; EXPLAIN shows index use for active students, subscriptions, support oldest-open, applications oldest-pending, tenants created/recent, license expiry; heavy grouped-users query now count(u.id): variant plan HashAggregate ~45 ms at 100k students vs 95 ms with a sort spill, bounded by the 2 s hint (UserRepository.OVERVIEW_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS) and the 60 s section cache. PERF-002 judged acceptable (QUAL-010). Not independently re-run by this reviewer.
verification_notes.conventions: Constructor DI, @Service/@Component consistent with HostDashboardService/HostOperationsSections, records plain data, DashboardSection/Runner reused, no unused imports in the new or edited files, no dead code (DashboardSection.forbidden() is now used), no public mutable state, named constants for limits/TTL/bucket parts in OverviewConstants (the Phase 3 block is appended after the Host block rather than grouped - cosmetic). Exception: the IllegalArgumentException message in DashboardCacheKeys.admin is an inline literal, matching the Phase 1 host() sibling. AdminCommercialSections.support() looks the tenant map up twice (containsKey + get) - trivial.
verification_notes.tests_coverage_skimmed: Present and aligned with the phase's test list: role matrix against the real PlatformOperationPolicy (admin, manager, academic manager/staff, legacy author), controller 200/403/400 with real method security, forbidden sections never touching facades or cache, bucket isolation and a planted none-bucket payload, per-section failure isolation, failed section not cached, cache TTL/keys, Jackson round trip of all 8 payloads, SeatUtilisationRanking edge cases (overflow guard, limit <= 0, ties), month boundaries with a fixed clock (VN vs UTC), batched statement counts for recent tenants / plan names / seat limits, derived-expiry boundaries, no description/code/email/tax keys in payloads. Test results were taken from tests/phase-03-test-report.json (308 new tests passed, only the pre-existing ModuleStructureTest failure remains with a violation set identical to baseline); this reviewer did not re-run tests or EXPLAIN.
